route_title: Optimization of Two-Layer SiO2/TiO2 Antireflection Coating Geometry

route_snapshot.title: Optimization of Two-Layer SiO2/TiO2 Antireflection Coating Geometry
route_snapshot.scientific_hypothesis: There exists a combination of layer order (SiO2-first or TiO2-first) and layer thicknesses within the 40-160 nm range that minimizes the arithmetic mean power reflectance below the soft target of 0.03 across the 450-700 nm band.
route_snapshot.design_principle: Destructive interference of reflected waves at the air-coating and coating-substrate interfaces. The optimal thicknesses depend on the refractive index contrast and the specific sequence of high/low index layers relative to the incident medium and substrate.
route_snapshot.proposed_topology: Air (n=1.0) / Layer 1 (Variable Material: sio2 or tio2, Variable Thickness) / Layer 2 (Variable Material: tio2 or sio2, Variable Thickness) / Glass Substrate (n=1.52). Exactly two layers total.
soft_objectives: minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance (450-700 nm, 5 nm step, s-pol, normal incidence)
manufacturing_considerations: Layer thickness must be strictly between 40 nm and 160 nm
Exactly one layer of SiO2 and one layer of TiO2 required
theory_basis: Transfer Matrix Method (TMM) for multilayer optics
Thin film interference conditions for broadband antireflection
expected_advantages: Directly addresses the user's specific material and thickness constraints
Explores the full feasible design space for the two-layer system
known_risks: The global minimum may lie outside the 40-160 nm thickness bounds
The fixed refractive indices may not allow a mean reflectance below 0.03 with only two layers
route_snapshot.execution_request_english: Perform a deterministic optimization using the Transfer Matrix Method (TMM) for a planar two-layer stack on a semi-infinite glass substrate (n=1.52, lossless) with air incidence (n=1.0). The stack must contain exactly one layer of 'SiO2 (Gao)' (n=1.46, lossless) and one layer of 'TiO2 (Siefke)' (n=2.40, lossless). Evaluate both possible layer orders: (1) Air/SiO2 (Gao)/TiO2 (Siefke)/Glass and (2) Air/TiO2 (Siefke)/SiO2 (Gao)/Glass. For each order, optimize the thickness of both layers, constrained between 40 nm and 160 nm inclusive. The objective is to minimize the arithmetic mean power reflectance for s-polarized light at normal incidence (0 degrees) over the wavelength range 450 nm to 700 nm, sampled every 5 nm. Use seed 17 for the optimizer. Allow a maximum of 64 solver evaluations per round. Report the best candidate's layer order, thicknesses, full reflectance spectrum, and the calculated mean reflectance. Do not claim the target (<0.03) is met without verifying the computed mean against the reported spectrum.

compilation_rationale: The request mandates evaluating two distinct layer orders (Air/SiO2/TiO2/Glass and Air/TiO2/SiO2/Glass) within a single optimization context. The bounded TMM task schema supports optimizing one fixed stack sequence per experiment. To proceed, please specify which of the two orders is the primary candidate for this draft, or confirm if you require two separate experiments to be generated.

route_snapshot.design_principle: Impedance matching via sequential quarter-wave-like transformations, where the low-index layer acts as an intermediate transformer between air and the high-index layer, which then matches to the substrate.
route_snapshot.proposed_topology: Air (n=1.0) | Layer 1: SiO2 (n=1.46) | Layer 2: TiO2 (n=2.40) | Substrate: Glass (n=1.52). Total finite layers: 2.
soft_objectives: minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance from 450 to 700 nm
achieve mean reflectance below 0.03 as a soft scoring preference
manufacturing_considerations: layer thickness must be between 40 and 160 nm
exactly one layer of SiO2 and one layer of TiO2 in this specific order
theory_basis: Transfer Matrix Method for multilayer interference
Quarter-wave antireflection coating theory generalized for two layers
expected_advantages: Provides a definitive optimal solution for the Low-High index sequence
Resolves the compilation ambiguity by fixing the topology

route_snapshot.execution_request_english: Perform a deterministic optimization using the Transfer Matrix Method for s-polarized light at normal incidence (0 degrees). The stack consists of exactly two finite layers on a semi-infinite glass substrate (n=1.52, lossless) with air incidence (n=1.0). The layer order is fixed: Layer 1 is SiO2 (n=1.46, lossless) and Layer 2 is TiO2 (n=2.40, lossless). Optimize the thickness of Layer 1 and Layer 2, both bounded between 40 nm and 160 nm. The objective is to minimize the arithmetic mean power reflectance sampled from 450 nm to 700 nm at 5 nm intervals. Use seed 17 for the optimizer and allow a maximum of 64 solver evaluations. Output the optimal thicknesses, the full reflectance spectrum, and the calculated mean reflectance. Canonical user controls: incidence angles 0 degrees. polarization s. wavelength intervals 450-700 nm. soft objectives: minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance from 450 to 700 nm; achieve mean reflectance below 0.03 as a soft scoring preference. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high reflection in the 450 to 700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: layer thickness must be between 40 and 160 nm; exactly one layer of SiO2 and one layer of TiO2.
